meta.sourcing_rules: Dates are only recorded from a region-specific source (the firm's own regional posting or careers page stating London). date_confidence: 'confirmed' = regional page/posting states this cycle explicitly; 'indicative' = regional source but rolling/prior-cycle/no year stated, or found via a search-engine summary of the regional posting rather than a direct fetch; 'unconfirmed' = no regional source seen yet, date fields left empty. Never alert on unconfirmed dates. Foreign-market (non-UK) dates are marked not_applicable rather than recorded. status: 'Speculative' is a fifth status alongside Open/Opens soon/Verify/Watch/Closed - for a real, London-relevant, small/boutique firm in scope (Consulting/Finance/AM/IB/Risk-Audit) where no live or historical Industrial Placement/Year-in-Industry posting could be found at all, but the firm is small enough that a direct, speculative approach (not an online application) is a realistic route in. Only add a Speculative entry when you can name a genuine reason the firm fits (sector, size, known to hire junior talent in some form) - never invent a firm with no real basis. eligibility for a Speculative entry should explain why no formal scheme was found; tactical_notes MUST include a concrete contact plan: who to approach (a named role, e.g. 'HR/Talent contact' or 'a partner in their [team] via LinkedIn'), which channel (email/LinkedIn InMail/phone), and what to lead with (a one-line pitch tailored to the firm, referencing Daniel's differentiators). Speculative entries never get invented dates and are excluded from the urgent-deadline alert logic the same as any unconfirmed-date role.
meta.fit_score_rubric: 1-5 scale, CV-match heuristic against each role's stated requirements: 5 = near-perfect alignment with no material gap (explicit requirement met by direct hands-on experience, not just adjacent exposure); 4 = strong alignment, thematic/sector fit is direct, but at least one requirement is met only by adjacent/observational experience rather than hands-on work product; 3 = decent alignment, meaningful gaps in either sector fit or demonstrated skill; 2 = weak alignment (wrong sub-sector, or the specific posting found is a poor match even if the firm is a good target); 1 = long shot. No role has yet scored 5 - see Daniel's standing note on how to close the gap to a 5, in profile.fit_improvement_notes.
meta.environment_notes: This run had no access to WebFetch against company/careers domains (blocked by the sandbox's egress proxy) and no Claude in Chrome/Edge browser extension (not available in this cloud session). Discovery relied on the Indeed connector (best source this run: real, dated, primary-sourced UK postings) plus WebSearch summaries of firm career pages (treated as 'indicative' unless the search result directly quoted primary posting text). ZipRecruiter is US/Canada-only per its own tool description and returned nothing usable for London. Dice returned no relevant matches. If a future run gains real WebFetch/browser access to career portals, re-verify 'indicative'/'Watch' entries and upgrade their date_confidence. Same-day follow-up pass (2026-09-01): user asked to broaden coverage to boutique/small firms and prior-year ('last year') cycles as a signal for reopening. Indeed/Dice/ZipRecruiter/Gmail connectors had been toggled off for this chat when reconnected mid-session (org shows them connected but enabledInChat:false) - re-enable in this chat's connector settings for a future pass to restore Indeed-quality primary sourcing. This pass relied entirely on WebSearch, so most new entries are tagged 'indicative' rather than 'confirmed'. Confirmed as explicitly non-London and excluded: Lloyds Banking Group Finance/Risk Industrial Placement Schemes (Bristol/Leeds/Edinburgh only, not London). Third same-day pass (2026-09-01): user asked to push into smaller/less-searchable boutiques and to check LinkedIn/Indeed specifically. The Indeed connector remained toggled off for this chat (not re-enabled by the user between passes) so this pass used WebSearch with site:linkedin.com/jobs and site:uk.indeed.com filters instead - these surfaced some real listings (e.g. Mako Trading via LinkedIn, Lazard via LinkedIn) but LinkedIn's own search/API wasn't directly queryable, so coverage there is shallower than a logged-in LinkedIn search would give; per the original brief, LinkedIn is best checked manually for alumni/referral leads. Many boutique-name searches this pass (Vendigital, 4C Associates, Argon & Co, EFESO, DC Advisory, Clearwater International, Arma Partners, Spayne Lindsay, Quayle Munro, Marshall Wace, Winton, Brevan Howard, Beazley, IMC Trading, Optiver, LCP) returned company-profile information only with no confirmed placement-year scheme, so were deliberately left untracked rather than guessed. target.instruction: Cast wide across every firm in scope, discovered fresh each run - never limited to a fixed shortlist.

fit_improvement_notes.why_capped_at_4: Every strong role so far (Nomura, UBS x3, BlackRock, Goldman Sachs) scores 4, not 5, for the same structural reason: BofA, Investec and Serve Legal all gave real exposure, but all three were observational or audit-based (shadowing, attending forums, testing compliance) rather than producing a hands-on technical work product (a model, a dataset, a piece of code, a written analysis with a number attached). Requirements sections in these postings increasingly ask for or reward exactly that kind of artefact.
highest_leverage_actions: Finish the Bloomberg Market Concepts course (currently in progress) and put the completion certificate on the CV/LinkedIn - this is the single fastest close of the 'hands-on' gap for IB/AM/trading roles (UBS, Nomura, BlackRock, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley).

Add one free, short, credentialed technical course that produces an artefact: CFI's free Intro to Financial Modeling course, or a basic SQL/Excel-for-finance course - name it explicitly on applications rather than just 'proficient in Excel'.

For Risk & Audit roles (Nomura, RSM, BDO, Grant Thornton, Moore Kingston Smith): mention specific tools if learned (Alteryx, Power BI, or even structured Excel-based control testing) - Serve Legal's audit work is a strong narrative, but naming a tool used to analyse or report on the 100+ audits (even a simple spreadsheet tracker) turns 'I did audits' into 'I built the reporting process for audits'.

Keep the 1st-class average through Year 2 and say so explicitly in applications ('on track for a First') - several of these postings only ask for a 2:1, so exceeding it is a genuine differentiator worth stating, not assuming it speaks for itself.

For consulting/Big 4 (Deloitte, KPMG, PwC, EY, PA Consulting, Cartesian): practice timed case interviews and numerical/verbal reasoning tests (Bright Network and GraduatesFirst both have free practice sets) - this doesn't change the fit score here (which measures CV-match, not interview readiness) but is the actual bottleneck once an application converts to an assessment centre, and the NextGenWorks/BDO mock assessment centre experience is worth naming directly in applications.

For boutique/Speculative-status firms specifically: a tailored, firm-specific pitch (naming a deal, a sector focus, or something concrete about the firm) plus a direct approach to a named person matters more than CV polish - see each Speculative entry's tactical_notes for the suggested angle.

Use LinkedIn manually (outside this dashboard, per the original brief) to find University of Liverpool alumni at target firms, and consider reaching back out to BofA/Investec contacts from the insight days for a referral into their structured programmes - a referral changes real odds more than any CV edit.

roles.tactical_notes: Direct match for the BofA financial-reporting/regulatory-forum background - arguably a stronger CV match than the Sales & Trading track. Apply to both if eligible; they appear to be separate processes.

roles.title: Actuarial Placement
roles.eligibility: Rare exact cohort match: this role starts summer 2027 and runs the 2027/28 academic year - the same window as Daniel's. However, it's explicitly for students studying an Actuarial or Mathematical (or closely related) degree - Business Management is a stretch fit here even with strong Year 1 stats/accounting marks, so treat as a long shot unless a more general-business-friendly variant exists.
roles.tactical_notes: Worth a direct look specifically because the dates line up exactly, which is rare this early - most other 2027-cohort-matching roles found so far are the UBS/Nomura set. No deadline found this run; check Bright Network's Travelers page directly.

roles.title: UK Placement Programme (Economics)
roles.eligibility: For high-achieving economics students; positions span micro, macro, scenarios, econometrics, data, real estate and environmental work. 2026 cycle found this run - wrong cohort. London is confirmed as one of the three UK locations (alongside Oxford and Belfast) - not guaranteed to be London-based specifically for every opening, so confirm the London option directly.
roles.tactical_notes: A genuinely boutique, specialist economics-consulting brand distinct from the Big-4/MBB crowd - good complement to FTI Consulting. Strong thematic fit with the 1st-class Statistics for Business Analytics and Economic Principles modules.
roles.source: WebSearch (Oxford Economics careers / Bright Network / Glassdoor, prior-cycle posting)

roles.title: HR Industrial Placement, London
roles.eligibility: This specific posting found is HR-focused, not front-office. Confirms Mako runs an Industrial Placement scheme in its London office (offices also in Amsterdam, Singapore, Sydney) - worth checking mako.com/early-careers directly for whether a Trading or Technology placement track also exists, which would be a stronger fit.
roles.tactical_notes: Genuinely small, less-searchable boutique - a specialist options market maker, not a household name, exactly the kind of firm a shortlist-based search would miss. Low fit score reflects the HR-specific posting found, not the firm generally.

roles.title: Industrial Placement (Actuarial)
roles.eligibility: Only evidence found for an actual 'Industrial Placement' (rather than graduate scheme or summer internship) is a stale 2020 posting - current 2026-2027 activity found is a Graduate Programme and Summer Internships only, both wrong scheme type for a Year-in-Industry placement. Unclear whether Hymans Robertson still runs a placement-year track at all.
roles.tactical_notes: Included despite weak evidence because the firm and London office are real and actuarial/pensions work fits the Risk category - but confirm directly (hymans.co.uk/careers) before spending real application effort here.

roles.title: Consulting (Operations & Improvement) Industrial Placement
roles.eligibility: Open to undergraduates with an industrial placement built into their course structure.
roles.tactical_notes: Third PA Consulting track found alongside Delivery and Business Design & Transformation. 2026 cycle (wrong cohort) found this run; PA Consulting runs annually.
